what_changed.headline: Energy shock is broadening inflation risk
what_changed.significance: Saudi Arabia shut the East-West pipeline after attacks; ECB commentary says the energy shock is likely longer-lasting, while refined-product prices reached new highs.
what_changed.transmission: Higher fuel and transport costs raise headline inflation and risk second-round effects, increasing pressure on central banks while weakening energy-importing economies.

what_changed.headline: US Fed hike expectations remain elevated ahead of Wednesday
what_changed.significance: Recent US core CPI was 0.29% month-on-month and headline CPI 3.4% year-on-year; several institutions expect or strongly favour a September hike.
what_changed.transmission: A hike may support the front end, but long yields remain exposed to issuance, real-rate and energy risks.

what_changed.headline: Europe is linking AI investment to productivity and monetary sovereignty
what_changed.significance: ECB officials highlight rapid AI adoption, infrastructure needs, dependence on US capacity and potential productivity gains, alongside correction and financing risks.
what_changed.transmission: AI investment supports capex and potential growth but competes with sovereign borrowing and leaves technology assets vulnerable to valuation corrections.

executive_decisions.development: Treat the energy shock as a cross-asset inflation and growth risk rather than a narrow oil trade.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: Supply disruption is occurring alongside already elevated refined-product prices and persistent central-bank concern.
executive_decisions.transmission: Energy-importing economies face weaker real income and higher inflation, raising policy risk and pressure on rates and cyclicals.

executive_decisions.development: Keep duration exposure selective around the Fed decision.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: A hike could validate higher front-end rates, but long-end yields also reflect issuance, productivity and geopolitical factors.
executive_decisions.transmission: The curve may steepen or bear-flatten depending on whether growth resilience or inflation credibility dominates.

themes.title: Energy shock versus policy credibility
themes.implication: Upside risk to front-end and inflation-sensitive rates; downside risk to energy-importing growth assets; dollar support is possible but not assured.

themes.title: AI investment, productivity and financing strain
themes.implication: Supports selective AI infrastructure exposure over the medium term but raises duration, credit and equity-correction risks.

themes.title: Energy supply shock becomes a policy shock
themes.implication: Near-term bias remains toward higher inflation risk, tighter policy expectations and pressure on duration; growth-sensitive assets remain vulnerable if the shock persists.

themes.title: AI investment supports activity but raises capital-intensity and valuation questions
themes.implication: Infrastructure beneficiaries may remain supported, while software and credit exposures require proof of monetisation.

themes.title: Energy shock meets restrictive policy
themes.implication: Policy rates can remain high even as growth weakens, increasing duration and cyclical-equity sensitivity.

themes.title: Long-end yield pressure is becoming a cross-asset constraint
themes.implication: Duration, credit and rate-sensitive equities remain vulnerable if yields continue higher.

themes.title: Energy shock versus disinflation
themes.implication: Prefer monitoring inflation-sensitive rates and margins over assuming a broad inflation spiral.

themes.title: AI investment cycle: strong demand, uncertain monetisation
themes.implication: The cycle supports semiconductors and selected infrastructure, while financing needs and model-price competition create credit and equity dispersion.

themes.title: Energy shock versus growth
themes.implication: Near-term inflation pressure favors caution on duration; growth deterioration would reverse that bias.

themes.title: Yen normalization and carry risk
themes.implication: Maintain vigilance on carry-sensitive exposures; continuation requires policy and flow support.

themes.title: Supply-driven inflation versus resilient demand
themes.implication: Rates risk remains asymmetric to the upside in the near term, while growth-sensitive assets face margin and real-income pressure.

themes.title: AI investment moves from capability to economics
themes.implication: AI exposure remains differentiated: infrastructure demand is supported, while cash generation, utilization and software defensibility become decisive.

themes.title: Energy scarcity is extending inflation and policy risk
themes.implication: Higher energy volatility can delay monetary easing, pressure rate-sensitive assets and support energy-linked commodities.

themes.title: Monetary-policy divergence is being tested by data
themes.implication: Front-end rates, the dollar and risk assets remain highly sensitive to CPI and central-bank decisions.

themes.title: Sovereign supply and market intermediation
themes.implication: Long-duration rates may remain vulnerable even if near-term policy expectations soften; liquidity conditions should be monitored rather than assumed benign.

themes.title: Fiscal and supply pressure at the long end
themes.implication: Long-end rates remain vulnerable, with knock-on pressure for property, small caps and speculative growth.

themes.title: AI investment remains structurally supported but increasingly selective
themes.implication: Prefer profitable cash generators and energy infrastructure over unprofitable, financing-dependent growth; market confirmation is unavailable.

themes.title: Supply-driven inflation versus restrictive policy
themes.implication: The combination can keep rates higher for longer while weakening real household income and cyclical demand.

themes.title: Global yield and fiscal-risk repricing
themes.implication: The shock is negative for duration and broad risk appetite, but its FX effect is ambiguous where higher yields are interpreted as fiscal rather than monetary strength.

themes.title: AI adoption is broadening, but near-term labour displacement remains limited
themes.implication: The evidence supports gradual labour transformation rather than an immediate employment shock, while investment exposure is more credible through infrastructure and productivity channels than through an assumed aggregate-demand boom.
